title: Service Continuity Terms of the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
## What this schedule fixes

For every service model of the Workplace Cafe Management Program, this schedule fixes the standby charge taken for each month of suspended service, expressed as a percentage of the monthly management fee; the ceiling on suspended calendar days allowed in one contract year; the shortest suspension a service model will accept, in calendar days; and the calendar days of notice needed to bring service back from suspension.

## Figures by service model

| Service model | Standby charge (per cent of monthly management fee) | Suspended-day ceiling per contract year (calendar days) | Minimum suspension (calendar days) | Resumption notice (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grab & Go Cafe Service | 25.0 | 30 | 5 | 3 |
| Limited Service Cafe | 30.0 | 45 | 7 | 5 |
| Full Service Cafe | 35.0 | 60 | 10 | 10 |
| Culinary Center Cafe | 40.0 | 75 | 14 | 14 |
| Executive Dining Service | 45.0 | 45 | 7 | 7 |
| Campus Dining Commons Service | 50.0 | 90 | 14 | 21 |

## Notes distinguishing the models

The standby charge climbs steadily from 25.0 per cent at Grab & Go Cafe Service to 50.0 per cent at Campus Dining Commons Service, tracking the larger fixed complement each heavier service model keeps in place through a suspension. The suspended-day ceiling and the minimum suspension widen together moving toward the larger models, with Executive Dining Service breaking that pattern by pairing the shorter ceiling and minimum of Limited Service Cafe with a standby charge above every other model. The resumption notice period does not simply track the ceiling: Full Service Cafe and Culinary Center Cafe each require a resumption notice equal to their own minimum suspension, while Campus Dining Commons Service requires a resumption notice of 21 calendar days, longer than its own minimum suspension of 14 calendar days.

## Reading the schedule, hypothetically

Suppose a site held under Full Service Cafe were suspended for 10 calendar days, the minimum this table allows that service model. The standby charge for the suspended month would be read from this table at 35.0 per cent of the monthly management fee, and bringing service back would, hypothetically, call for the 10 calendar days of resumption notice this table fixes for that service model.
